title: Best Stand Mixers for Holiday Baking (2026)
summary: Hand-mixing cookie dough for a holiday crowd wrecks your forearms, and a weak mixer that stalls on bread dough wrecks the bake. We narrowed it to 4 stand mixers that independent testers rate well, from the all-round winner to the budget pick and two heavy-duty bread machines. Pick wrong and you will fight your mixer every time the dough gets thick.
method: We started from CNN Underscored's hands-on test of nine stand mixers, where every model made the same buttercream, crusty bread loaf and cookie dough, and from Homes & Gardens' expert tests for bread dough. We ranked machines on mixing, kneading, whipping, stability, noise, cleanup and warranty. Each pick below suits a different kind of baker.
assumptions: Prices change often, so check the current price on Amazon before you buy. Warranty terms come from the testers' write-ups, so confirm them with the brand when you buy.
intro: The biggest difference between stand mixers is what happens when the dough gets thick. In CNN Underscored's test, how well a mixer handled wet, sticky dough while still mixing evenly set the winners apart from the rest.
Black Friday is Nov 27, and stand mixers like these are often marked down around then. We re-check Amazon prices every day, so the price on each card is the current one when you read this.

voices.name: KitchenAid Artisan 5-Quart
voices.src: CNN Underscored · our note on the catch
voices.like: It beat the other mixers in all three of their recipe tests: cookie dough, bread and frosting.
voices.catch: At 26 pounds it is heavy to lift on and off the counter, and the whisk has to be hand-washed.

voices.name: Cuisinart SM-50
voices.src: CNN Underscored · our note on the catch
voices.like: It mixed far better than the ultra-budget models they tested, even with thick cookie dough and slack bread dough.
voices.catch: Its whisk was a poor fit for the bowl, so they had to stop and scrape down more often.

tips.title: 5 mistakes that make a stand mixer a bad buy
items: In CNN Underscored's test, the very small and very cheap models struggled with cookie dough and bread dough, and one performed like an undersized hand mixer.
Heavier mixers stay put on the counter when the dough gets thick. If you bake bread or cookies often, look for a stronger motor (325 watts or more) and some heft.
Not checking what is in the box.
Most mixers ship with a paddle, a dough hook and a whisk, but some, like the Bosch Universal Plus, leave out cookie paddles you will want for cookie dough.
Picking tilt-head when you make big bread batches.
Bowl-lift and base-motor designs handle heavier dough with less rocking, and they leave the top open for adding ingredients.
The testers noted warranties from 1 year up to 7 years on the Ankarsrum motor. On a $400+ appliance, that is worth a look.

faq: What is the best stand mixer for most people?
The KitchenAid Artisan 5-Quart. It won all three of CNN Underscored's recipe tests and has the widest range of attachments.
Is the Cuisinart SM-50 good enough?
If you want to start baking without paying KitchenAid money, yes. It handled thick cookie dough and slack bread dough well in testing, but its whisk is awkward.
Which mixer is best for bread dough?
The Bosch Universal Plus and the Ankarsrum Original are the heavy-duty choices. Both have the motor in the base, which suits large batches and stiff dough.
Is the Ankarsrum worth the price?
Only if you bake bread several times a week or in large batches. CNN Underscored called it probably more machine than most people need.
Tilt-head gives easier access to the bowl and beater. Bowl-lift and base-motor designs are steadier with heavy dough.

products.name: KitchenAid Artisan Series 5-Quart Tilt-Head Stand Mixer
products.desc: 5-quart tilt-head mixer with a 10-speed motor, a stainless steel bowl and a pouring shield. It comes with a paddle, dough hook and whisk, and it works with dozens of attachments through a front power hub.
products.benefit: If you bake for holidays, birthdays or weekend treats, this takes the hardest work off your arms: it creamed butter and sugar, kneaded a crusty bread loaf and whipped fluffy frosting better than the other eight mixers CNN Underscored tested. It is heavy enough to stay put on the counter, and later you can add attachments like a pasta roller or meat grinder instead of buying more gadgets.
why: It beat the competition in every one of CNN Underscored's recipe tests.
The paddle and dough hook are dishwasher-safe, and the bowl locks in quickly.
specs: Paddle, dough hook, whisk and pouring shield included
Front power hub for dozens of attachments
pros: Best mixing and kneading in testing
Huge range of attachments and colors
cons: Heavy to lift on and off the counter
Costs noticeably more than the Cuisinart
products.best_for: Home bakers who want one reliable mixer for cookies, cakes and the occasional bread
products.skip_if: you bake bread several times a week or in very large batches, since a heavy-duty bread mixer will suit you better

products.name: Cuisinart SM-50 Precision Master Stand Mixer
products.desc: 5.5-quart tilt-head mixer with a 12-speed motor, a three-year limited warranty and a choice of 11 colors. It weighs about 18 pounds.
products.benefit: If you want to start baking without paying KitchenAid money, this still handles thick cookie dough and slack bread dough with a motor that is not noisy. At 18 pounds it is easy to move around the kitchen. Its three-year warranty adds some peace of mind, and the trade-off is a whisk that needs more scraping.
why: CNN Underscored named it the best affordable stand mixer, and it mixed significantly better than the ultra-budget models.
It is lighter than most full-size mixers but stays steady while mixing.
specs: 11 color options and five extra attachments
pros: Quiet for the power it has
cons: Whisk fits the bowl poorly, so you will scrape more
Not as strong as the top performers
products.best_for: New bakers and budget-minded home cooks
products.skip_if: you plan to knead heavy bread dough every week

products.name: Bosch Universal Plus Stand Mixer
products.badge: Best for Bread and Big Batches
products.desc: Base-motor mixer with an 800-watt motor, a 6.5-quart plastic bowl and four speeds plus pulse. It weighs about 17 pounds, has suction-cup feet and works with more than 20 accessories.
products.benefit: If you make bread, bagels or big batches of dough, this takes the load that makes other mixers strain, and you can knead a lot of dough in one go. The motor sits in the base, so the top stays open for adding ingredients. CNN Underscored ranked it near the top for performance, but you will want to budget for cookie paddles because they are not in the box.
why: CNN Underscored said it shone with bread dough, kneading it quickly into good elasticity.
The bottom-drive design suits large batches and has a three-year motor warranty.
specs: Three-year motor warranty, more than 20 accessories
cons: Unusual design takes getting used to
products.best_for: Frequent bread bakers and anyone making large batches
products.skip_if: you mostly bake small batches of cookies and want a classic, familiar mixer

products.name: Ankarsrum Original Kitchen Machine
products.desc: Swedish base-motor mixer with an 8-quart stainless steel bowl, a 600-watt variable-speed motor, a dough roller and a separate scraper. It comes with a seven-year motor warranty.
products.benefit: If you bake bread several times a week or for a big family, it kneads large batches in an 8-quart bowl while staying quiet. The seven-year motor warranty and wide attachment range mean it can last you for years. CNN Underscored also called it probably more machine than most people need, so only buy it if you bake that often.
why: CNN Underscored found it quiet and amply powered, and a fit for bakers making large batches of bread several times a week.
Homes & Gardens' tester said it felt like having an artisan baker helping in the kitchen.
specs: 8-quart stainless steel bowl, plus a 6.5-quart plastic bowl
Attachments for juicing, pasta, grain milling and more
cons: The most expensive mixer in the test
Hard to add dry ingredients without getting them on the central parts
Learning curve and an unusual design
products.best_for: Serious bread bakers who bake several times a week
products.skip_if: you bake only now and then, because it is more machine than you need
